first_impression.reaction: Corfu came up after Crete, so I searched it. The opener goes straight to geography and a sorting rule: 'The right area depends on how many guests you are inviting, the kind of ceremony you want and the view you want behind you when you say your vows.' No 'island paradise'. The guest-count takeaway (eight guests up to 250) tells me straight away this list will help me cross things off for 60 to 90. Kept reading.

journey.quote: Every venue here says on its own site that it hosts weddings, and describes its sea view in its own words.
journey.reaction: Read this twice. Is that a disclaimer? It makes me wonder whether anyone from your side has actually stood on these terraces, or if this is a desk summary of ten websites. It's the second paragraph, so it colours everything after it.

journey.quote: Exclusive use means different things here, from a privately hired estate such as The Courti Estate to Atlantica's promise of one wedding on your day, so ask each venue which one it is offering.
journey.reaction: This is the fine print that turns into a nasty surprise later. Lawyer brain approves of a real example, not just a warning.

journey.section: Corfu wedding venues at a glance (table)
journey.quote: It is not a ranking. "Not published" means the venue does not state the detail on its own site.
journey.reaction: Good, no paid-placement 'best of' feel. But when I run down the capacity column for 60 to 90 people, most of it says 'Not published' or tops out at 30 or 50. Honest, but it leaves me with very few venues I can confirm actually fit us.

journey.quote: Atlantica asks couples marrying there to arrive at least three working days before the wedding and stay two working days after.
journey.reaction: That's the kind of detail I'd never have thought to ask, and it changes our leave planning. Exactly what I want from a guide.

journey.section: Choosing an area: east or west coast
journey.quote: Ask any venue with an exposed ceremony spot what its plan is on a windy afternoon.
journey.reaction: Nobody else mentions wind. Practical, and it's the sort of thing that goes wrong on the day with no one accountable.

journey.section: Choosing an area: east or west coast
journey.quote: A simple rule: if your guests want the Old Town on their doorstep, look at Kommeno and Corfu Town. If you want a resort that runs the whole week, look south-east or west. If you want the place to yourselves, start with the two private houses.
journey.reaction: This is the paragraph I'd screenshot for James. A clear opinion at last.

journey.section: Kalami and the north-east / San Antonio
journey.quote: [San Antonio](https://sanantoniocorfuresort.gr/events/) invites couples to "say 'I do' with the Ionian breeze in your hair", or to renew their vows, "against a sensational backdrop of Greek blue, rugged rocks, and sea foam".
journey.reaction: I know it's the resort's line, but leading the section with it makes the page sound like a brochure. Same with 'cinematic sunsets' and 'sun-kissed terraces' elsewhere. A lot of the venue sections are stitched-together venue quotes rather than your view.

journey.section: Kalami and the north-east / San Antonio
journey.quote: Kalami is the village the Durrell family chose as their home while Gerald Durrell wrote his best-known books, and the resort looks straight onto it.
journey.reaction: Mum would love this. A real reason to pick a place, not just another sea view.

journey.quote: Outdoor receptions start from 20:30, and outdoor music stops at 23:30, after which the party can move indoors to the main restaurant until 04:00 at the latest. Fireworks are not allowed.
journey.reaction: Actual house rules with times. This is the insider detail I want for every venue, and the 2023 date warning next to it is honest.

journey.quote: Vertigo Sky Bar, the large space, runs a shorter season than the garden, so a shoulder-season wedding for more than 30 guests needs a plan built around Oribu Restaurant for the reception.
journey.reaction: This is a real trade-off for our numbers and a May or October date. Very useful. Angsana is one of the few that clearly fits 60 to 90.

journey.quote: Because the ceremony venues are listed as symbolic, a couple wanting a legally registered marriage should plan the civil step separately.
journey.reaction: Separately how? At a town hall in Corfu before the ceremony? Back in Sydney? This is the one venue that fits our size, and this sentence leaves the legal side hanging.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms them in writing for your date.
journey.reaction: Some version of this closes every area, five times. I got it the first time. By Ermones it feels like a template and a sales nudge between sections.

journey.section: Getting to Corfu for your wedding
journey.quote: The airport sits close to most of this list. Rodostamo, on Kommeno Bay, is 11 km from the airport and 10 km from Corfu Town, and Atlantica Grand Mediterraneo on the west coast is about 25 minutes from the airport and town.
journey.reaction: Good start, and the rest-day tip is sensible. But no drive time for Kalami, Angsana or The Courti Estate, which are the ones I'd worry about for the grandparents.

journey.quote: For a summer date, that means a shaded ceremony spot, a later start, water for guests and an indoor or covered fallback agreed with the venue in advance.
journey.reaction: Heat and wildfires handled calmly with what to actually do. The month table goes straight to Mum and Dad.

journey.quote: The full steps for marrying in Greece as Australians are in [our guide to Greece wedding venues](https://weddedwonderland.com/destination-weddings/greece-wedding-venues#getting-legally-married-in-greece-as-australians-in-brief).
journey.reaction: The section is titled 'in Corfu' but it's mostly general Smartraveller and Athens embassy material, then sends me elsewhere for the steps. Nothing about where on Corfu the civil part actually happens.

journey.section: Shortlist your Corfu venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: One person and AUD quotes speak to two of my fears: being passed around, and currency surprises. Still doesn't say who is there on the day.

unanswered_questions: Has anyone from Wedded Wonderland actually been to these venues, or planned a wedding at one? Is there a real Corfu wedding with venue and date I can look at?
For 60 to 90 guests, half flying from Australia, which two or three of these ten would you actually shortlist?
How long is the drive from Corfu Airport to Kalami, Angsana Corfu and The Courti Estate?
If our ceremony venue is symbolic only, where and when does the legal civil step happen on Corfu, and do we both need to be there in person?
Is our Wedded Advisor, or someone you are accountable for, physically on Corfu on the wedding day?
Do you arrange guest transfers from the airport, or just advise on them?

turn_offs_found.turn_off: Clichés: fairytale, dream day, say I do in paradise
turn_offs_found.quote: [San Antonio](https://sanantoniocorfuresort.gr/events/) invites couples to "say 'I do' with the Ionian breeze in your hair", or to renew their vows, "against a sensational backdrop of Greek blue, rugged rocks, and sea foam".
turn_offs_found.why: It's quoted from the resort, but it opens the section and is the exact 'say I do' phrasing I scroll past. Combined with 'cinematic sunsets' and 'sun-kissed terraces', it drags a measured guide toward brochure copy. Paraphrasing or moving the quote below the facts would fix it.

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms them in writing for your date.
turn_offs_found.why: Reassuring once, but repeated at the end of every area on top of three linked CTAs it reads as a nudge between sections rather than advice, and the template feel makes me wonder if a person is behind it.

would_share_with: James (partner): the at-a-glance table and the 'simple rule' paragraph, so we can rule areas in or out together
Mum and Dad (contributing): the weather table, the heat and wildfire paragraph, and the Durrell detail at Kalami
James again: the Corfu Palace house rules, as the benchmark for what to ask every other venue

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [shortlist your Corfu venues with a Wedded Advisor](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=corfu-wedding-venues&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: The tone is right, not pushy. But I'd want to see one real Corfu or Greece wedding you've done, and I'm not yet sure you know these places beyond their websites.

top_3_changes: Cut the intro line 'Every venue here says on its own site that it hosts weddings, and describes its sea view in its own words' (and its echo opening 'How to compare'); it reads as a disclaimer that you haven't seen the venues, and the brand voice doesn't need it.
Say once, strongly, that the Wedded Advisor confirms house rules in writing, and drop most of the five repeated area closers; lead San Antonio with facts instead of the resort's 'say I do' line.
Add airport drive times for Kalami, Angsana and The Courti Estate, and explain what 'plan the civil step separately' means in practice for a symbolic-only venue like Angsana.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Sophie (planner_couple), using persona voice and concerns
No invented brand facts; missing details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments and VERIFY markers ignored
Title, business details and absent prices treated as not must-fix; no requests for sourcing lines, per orchestrator

open_questions.question: The intro and 'How to compare' both state venues describe their sea views 'in their own words'. To this reader it reads as a sourcing disclaimer, which the brand voice avoids. Worth an editor pass to remove rather than add?

assumptions: Arrived from a Google search for 'corfu wedding venues' during early destination research; no other context was given.
Skimmed venues that can't confirm a fit for 60 to 90; read the table, comparison, area, Angsana, Corfu Palace, season and legal sections closely.
Family details (grandparents, parents contributing) are persona colour, not brand facts.
The persona card is provisional (not CRM-calibrated).
